Per-criterion status of every row

Source: R/criteria-status.R
criteria_status.Rd

Returns one row per row of the starting data and one logical column per criterion, recording whether the row passed (TRUE), failed (FALSE), or has no result (NA) for that criterion. Use it to audit who failed what, or to plot overlapping exclusion reasons, which the step-by-step cascade hides. To get the cohort itself, use cohort().

Usage

criteria_status(
  flow,
  mode = c("cumulative", "independent"),
  sets = c("pass", "fail"),
  na = c("keep", "false", "drop"),
  names = c("label", "step"),
  drop_randomise = TRUE,
  keep_data = FALSE,
  as = c("tibble", "data.table", "matrix")
)

Arguments

flow

A cf_flow object produced by apply_criteria().

mode

"cumulative" (default) or "independent"; see the section "Modes".

sets

"pass" (default) reports whether each row passed each criterion; "fail" negates every criterion column (NA stays NA), so TRUE marks the reasons a row fails.

na

What to do with NA in the criterion columns, applied after sets: "keep" (default) leaves them; "false" replaces them with FALSE; "drop" removes rows with any NA.

names

Criterion column names: "label" (default) uses step labels, made unique with a warning if repeated; "step" uses cf_step_<n>. A name that clashes with an id or data column is made unique with a warning.

drop_randomise

Logical. Omit randomise() steps (default TRUE).

keep_data

Logical. Include the original data columns between the id column(s) and the criterion columns (default FALSE).

as

Return type: "tibble" (default), "data.table" (requires the data.table package), or "matrix", a logical matrix of the criterion columns only, with the row identifier as row names (keep_data is ignored).

Value

For "tibble" and "data.table": the id column(s) given as id to apply_criteria() (or .cf_row_id if none was given), then the data columns if keep_data = TRUE, then one logical column per criterion in step order. Rows are in the original data order. For "matrix": a logical matrix.

Modes

Valuemode = "cumulative"mode = "independent"
TRUEReached the step and passed itThe criterion holds for the row
FALSERemoved at this stepThe criterion fails for the row
NANot assessed: removed at an earlier stepThe predicate gave NA, or a grouped step's by is NA

Cumulative mirrors the cascade used by cohort(), excluded() and the CONSORT diagram, and is built from the recorded steps without re-evaluating anything. Each row has at most one FALSE. NA means the row never reached that criterion, which is not the same as failing it; it only becomes FALSE if you ask for that with na = "false". Missing predicate values follow the cascade: an include() that evaluates to NA removes the row (FALSE), an exclude() that evaluates to NA keeps it (TRUE).

Independent evaluates every criterion against the full starting data, ignoring earlier steps, so a row can fail several criteria. Bear in mind:

  • group_include(), group_exclude() and select_within() depend on which rows are in each group. Evaluated on the full data, a group can pass or fail differently than it did in the cascade, where earlier steps had already removed some of its rows.

  • In a continue_criteria() flow, columns joined at a later stage are NA for rows excluded before the join, so later-stage predicates are usually NA for those rows.

  • randomise() steps are all TRUE (in cumulative mode they are TRUE where reached and NA otherwise). They are dropped by default.

Set plots

Set and overlap plots (e.g. the eulerr, UpSetR or ComplexUpset packages) take a membership matrix with no missing values. The usual question is how exclusion reasons overlap, so ask for failures and decide what NA means:

m <- criteria_status(flow, mode = "independent", sets = "fail",
                     na = "false", as = "matrix")
# eulerr::euler(m); UpSetR::upset(as.data.frame(m * 1))

See also

cohort() for the cohort itself, excluded() for removed rows.

Other flow accessors: cohort(), excluded(), stack_cohorts()

Examples

dat  <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 200, seed = 1)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Adults only") |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew consent")
flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit, id = "participant_id")

criteria_status(flow)
#> # A tibble: 200 × 4
#>    participant_id `Adults only` `Passed screening` `Withdrew consent`
#>    <chr>          <lgl>         <lgl>              <lgl>             
#>  1 P0001          TRUE          FALSE              NA                
#>  2 P0002          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  3 P0003          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  4 P0004          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  5 P0005          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  6 P0006          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  7 P0007          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  8 P0008          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#>  9 P0009          TRUE          FALSE              NA                
#> 10 P0010          TRUE          TRUE               TRUE              
#> # ℹ 190 more rows

# How often each exclusion reason applies, counting overlaps
m <- criteria_status(flow, mode = "independent", sets = "fail",
                     na = "false", as = "matrix")
colSums(m)
#>      Adults only Passed screening Withdrew consent 
#>                6               17                7
